# Pawty

> Pawty is a free, gamified dog training app for iPhone and Android, described as "Duolingo for dogs". It has 99 training skills in 3-minute sessions, 32 behaviour guides, streaks that freeze instead of reset, and a care calendar. No subscription, no paywall, no trial. It is made in Slovenia and available in 11 languages.

Key facts:

- Platforms: iPhone (App Store id 6805087382) and Android (Google Play package com.pawty).
- Languages: English, German, Spanish, French, Croatian, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian and Slovenian. The website has the same pages in each language under /de/, /es/, /fr/, /hr/, /it/, /nl/, /pl/, /pt/, /ro/ and /sl/.
- Training: 99 skills from sit and recall to tricks and agility, each with steps, common mistakes and a goal. Sessions last 3 minutes and are rated 1 to 5 paws. 3 perfect sessions in a row mark a skill as mastered. A 12-week puppy plan has review weeks built in.
- Motivation: daily streaks that freeze instead of reset after a missed day, 36 badges, experience points and a worldwide leaderboard.
- Behaviour: 32 guides on problems such as puppy biting, barking, pulling on the lead, resource guarding and recall, each with why it happens, what works and what makes it worse.
- Care: care calendar for vaccinations, grooming and dog school, food diary, equipment checklist.
- Method: positive reinforcement only, no aversive tools. Content is educational, not veterinary or behavioural advice.
- Business model: free, supported by banner advertising in the app and by affiliate commissions from the in-app Marketplace of pet retailers. The website shows no adverts.
- Data: stored with Supabase in Frankfurt, Germany. Website statistics use PostHog in the EU in cookieless mode.
- Operator: Matej Mesko, Slovenia. Contact: info@pawtyapp.com.

## Behaviour guides

- [Dog chasing cars, bikes and wildlife](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/chasing.html): A hardwired motor pattern that is self-rewarding. Management first, because every chase strengthens it.
- [Dog pawing, whining and nudging for attention](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/attention-seeking.html): Even annoyed attention counts. Flipping the maths so calm pays and pushy does not.
- [Dog will not settle in the evening](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/evening-settling.html): Evening restlessness usually means the day was under- or over-stimulating. A wind-down ritual that works.
- [Why does my puppy bite? Puppy mouthing explained](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/puppy-biting.html): Puppies bite to explore and learn bite control. Why the shark phase happens, what stops it, and what makes it worse.
- [Puppy teething: chewing during the teeth change](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/puppy-teething.html): 28 puppy teeth out, 42 adult teeth in, between 3 and 7 months. Which chews help sore gums and which are dangerous.
- [Adult dog chewing furniture out of boredom](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/adult-chewing.html): Chewing is self-soothing. What an under-stimulated adult dog is telling you, and how to redirect it.
- [Dog jumping up on people: how to stop it](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/jumping-up.html): Jumping is excitement plus a history of being paid for it. The 4-paws rule and the incompatible job that replaces it.
- [Dog pulling on the lead: why it happens and what works](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/pulling-on-lead.html): Dogs pull because it moved them forward. Stop-and-go, paying at your leg, and why prong collars create new problems.
- [Dog barking at the doorbell](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/barking-at-doorbell.html): The bell predicts an exciting event. How to recondition it so the bell predicts cheese instead of chaos.
- [Dog barking at other dogs on walks](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/barking-at-other-dogs.html): Usually frustration or discomfort. Finding the distance where your dog stays calm, and closing it over weeks.
- [Demand barking: dog barking at you for food or attention](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/demand-barking.html): The dog barks because it has worked before. Why it gets louder before it gets better.
- [Puppy whining at night: what actually helps](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/puppy-crying-at-night.html): Night crying is separation distress, not manipulation. Why cry-it-out erodes trust at this age.
- [Puppy crying in the crate](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/crate-crying.html): Confinement is unnatural until the crate is trained as a den. Open-door games and second-by-second progress.
- [Dog struggles being left alone](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/home-alone.html): Being alone is a learned skill, not a factory setting. Training absences in tiny doses, and when to film the dog.
- [Dog digging in the garden](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/digging.html): Digging is hardwired. You cannot delete it, you can relocate it to a legal dig zone.
- [Counter surfing: dog stealing food from worktops](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/counter-surfing.html): The counter paid out once. Why airtight management, not training, is the actual cure.
- [Dog eating poo (coprophagia)](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/eating-poo.html): Common, rarely diet-related. Instant pickup, Leave it, and the vet check worth doing.
- [Dog eating things on walks](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/eating-things-on-walks.html): Dogs are opportunistic scavengers by design. Street-level Leave it, and when a basket muzzle is a safety tool.
- [Resource guarding: early signs over food and toys](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/resource-guarding.html): Freezing, hard stare or a growl means fear of loss. Why you must never punish a growl.
- [Lead reactivity: dog lunging and barking on the lead](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/lead-reactivity.html): Big feelings with no escape option. Working below threshold, and progress measured in metres per month.
- [Dog scared of fireworks and thunderstorms](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/fear-of-fireworks.html): Preparing a den, why comforting your dog is fine, and the sound work to start in November.
- [Dog not coming when called](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/recall-problems.html): The environment pays better than you. Rebuilding recall on a long line, and protecting the cue.
- [Puppy toilet training accidents](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/toilet-training.html): A puppy bladder holds roughly its age in months in hours. Timing, and why enzymatic cleaner matters.
- [Dog marking indoors](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/marking-indoors.html): Small deliberate deposits on vertical spots. Rule out medical causes first.
- [A female dog's first heat: what to expect](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/first-heat.html): Between 6 and 15 months, lasting 2 to 4 weeks. Management for 3 weeks, then life resumes.
- [Dog humping: what it actually means](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/humping.html): Mostly over-arousal and stress relief, not dominance and often not sexual.
- [Zoomies explained (frenetic random activity periods)](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/zoomies.html): Sudden racing laps are a normal, healthy energy release. Manage the terrain, not the joy.
- [Dog begging at the table](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/begging.html): Those eyes once earned a chip. A true zero-payout policy, and training the humans.
- [Dog stealing socks and running off with them](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/stealing-and-running.html): Grab a sock, humans erupt into a chase. Killing the chase economy.
- [Dog scared of car rides](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/car-fear.html): Motion sickness, or the car only ever drives to the vet. Rebuilding in steps.
- [Puppy peeing when excited or greeting people](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/excited-peeing.html): Immature bladder control, not spite. Why punishment makes submissive peeing worse.
- [Dog hates nail trimming](https://pawtyapp.com/guides/nail-trimming.html): One painful quick-cut creates a long memory. Cooperative care, one nail a day.

## Blog

- [How long should puppy walks be?](https://pawtyapp.com/post-walks.html): The 5-minutes-per-month puppy walk rule, what counts toward it, and how to read your puppy.
- [Teach your dog to sit in a week](https://pawtyapp.com/post-sit.html): The lure method for teaching sit, the 2 classic mistakes, and what success looks like per session.
- [Puppy teething survival guide](https://pawtyapp.com/post-teething.html): Teething timeline months 3 to 7, the relief menu, and the mistakes to avoid.
- [Why 5 minutes a day beats weekend marathons](https://pawtyapp.com/post-5minutes.html): Short daily dog training sessions beat long weekend ones: repetitions, spaced learning and streaks.
- [What a puppy actually costs in the first year](https://pawtyapp.com/post-puppy-cost.html): Line-by-line European costs for a puppy's first year: crate, vet, food, grooming and insurance, with what you can safely skip.
- [The puppy shopping list, and what you can skip](https://pawtyapp.com/post-shopping-list.html): What to buy before a puppy arrives, what to buy in month 2, and the 6 things pet shops sell that you do not need.
- [The puppy vaccination schedule in Europe](https://pawtyapp.com/post-vaccination.html): The standard European puppy vaccination timetable, what each vaccine covers, and how to socialise safely before the course is finished.
- [How much sleep does a puppy need](https://pawtyapp.com/post-puppy-sleep.html): Puppies need 18 to 20 hours of sleep a day. Why the evening biting is overtiredness, and how to enforce a nap without a fight.
- [Clicker or marker word: which should you use](https://pawtyapp.com/post-clicker-vs-marker.html): Both mark the exact moment your dog gets it right. Which to use when, how to load it in 2 minutes, and the 4 mistakes.
- [Cockapoo grooming: what nobody tells you](https://pawtyapp.com/post-cockapoo-grooming.html): Curly coats never stop growing. The real yearly cost, why matting happens, and the line-brushing method that prevents it.
- [Adopting an adult rescue dog: the 3-3-3 rule](https://pawtyapp.com/post-rescue-333.html): 3 days, 3 weeks, 3 months. What settling in actually looks like for an adult rescue dog, and what to do in each phase.
- [Fireworks and your dog: start preparing now](https://pawtyapp.com/post-fireworks.html): How to prepare a dog for New Year fireworks: sound training from November, a safe den, the night itself, and when to see the vet.
- [Christmas dangers for dogs: what to keep out of reach](https://pawtyapp.com/post-christmas-dangers.html): The Christmas foods, decorations and plants that are dangerous for dogs, and what to do if your dog ate something.
- [Snuffle mats: why 10 minutes of sniffing tires a dog out](https://pawtyapp.com/post-snuffle-mat.html): Why sniffing tires and calms a dog, how to use a snuffle mat step by step, and sniffing games without one.
- [Winter paw care: salt, ice and cold](https://pawtyapp.com/post-winter-paws.html): Protect your dog's paws in winter: rinsing off road salt, paw balm, ice balls between the toes, coats and winter dangers.
- [Travelling in the EU with your dog: pet passport and rules](https://pawtyapp.com/post-eu-travel.html): The EU pet travel rules: microchip, rabies vaccination, the 21-day wait, the pet passport, tapeworm rules and travel tips.
